persona.bio: Beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, paid partly on commission. Makeovers and color matching, restocking testers, cleaning the counter, keeping her client book, texting her clients when new launches come in or there's a gift with purchase, hitting her sales goals, events on weekends. Texting clients and keeping the client book take the most time outside makeovers. She texts clients from her own iPhone. She tried an AI app once and didn't trust it. Her store restricts AI.

steps.note: I work as a beauty advisor at a department store makeup counter, and part of my pay is commission. I text my clients from my phone about new launches, held items, gifts with purchase and follow ups after a visit. My clients are regulars and new customers, and I want every message to sound warm, short and like me. Keep replies to a few sentences. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, shades, dates, offers or stock. Use square brackets for anything I need to fill in. Never claim a product does something I did not say. Give me the text only, ready for me to read and change before I send it.

steps.title: Your follow up texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your follow up texts live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. You stop starting from your client book every time, and you only fill in the name, shade or day. Every text still sounds like you, because the words are yours.

Hi [first name]! Just checking in on the [product] you picked up. Any questions on how to apply it? Happy to show you again when you stop by.
Hi [first name]! We have a launch coming on [day]: [product]. Would you like me to save you one? I can also set up a time to try it.
Hi [first name]! Thank you for stopping by [day]. I’d love to see you again soon. Text me when you’re free and I’ll save you a spot at the counter.

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, phone number, address or purchase history into a chat tool.
Use square brackets in place of names and details, and fill them in yourself on your phone.
Don’t paste your client book or sales numbers into a chat tool.
Check every text for the right product, shade, offer and day before you send it.
Only use AI for work tasks once your company says it is okay.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I’d like to know which AI tools the company has approved and what I may use them for. I’m thinking of using one to help write my follow up texts to clients and my replies to their messages, without ever typing client names or details into it. I would read every text before sending it. Could you let me know what is allowed, or point me to the right person in IT?

design.today: You write these many times a day, often starting from your client book each time. You start from the paper client book, the Notes app or the last text thread.
design.newWay: Because your company restricts AI, AI does not touch this work. Instead you set up a small set of your own follow up texts, written by you, so each one is a few letters away on your phone. You open the client book, pick the matching text, add the name, shade and day yourself, and send it. The wording is already yours, so you stop starting from scratch each time.

steps.goal: Pick the four or five follow up texts you send most, such as a launch note, a held shade, and a thank you after a visit.
Write each one yourself in your own voice, with clear gaps for the name, product and day.
Keep the finished texts in one note, titled so you can find it fast between clients.
Once a month, read the note again and remove any text you no longer use or that no longer fits a launch.

material.label: Follow up text set
material.what: Your own four or five most common follow up texts, written by you, with gaps for name, product and day.

material.label: Gap checklist
material.what: A short list of what to fill in before sending: name, shade, hold day and any gift with purchase detail.

design.checkPoint: You read each text and fill in every gap before you send it yourself from your phone.

design.today: You answer client texts many times a day, one at a time from scratch.
design.newWay: Because your company restricts AI, AI does not touch this work. You keep a short list of your own answers to the questions clients ask most, so you are not writing each reply from scratch. When a text comes in, you pick the matching answer, adjust it for that client and send it. Your replies stay in your voice and stay accurate, and the common ones take far less thought.

steps.goal: Look back through your recent client texts and choose the ten questions you hear most, like stock, holds, shade help and gift with purchase.
Write one short answer to each question in your own words, with a gap wherever the answer depends on the client.
Save the ten answers in one note so you can copy the right one quickly.
Mark any question that needs a real conversation, so you answer it in person or by hand.

material.label: Ten common answers
material.what: Your own written replies to the ten questions clients ask most, with gaps for client details.

material.label: Answer by hand list
material.what: A short list of question types you always answer personally, such as skin concerns or price disputes.

design.checkPoint: You read each reply against the client's question and fill in any gaps before you press send.
